extracted.intended_audience: public relations instructors and students (higher education PR writing courses)
extracted.subtask_description: An instructional-model guidance for integrating computer technology (primarily word processing) into public relations writing courses to improve the writing process, management skills, teamwork, and creativity. The model articulates four instructional objectives and recommended lab/staffing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make the computer disappear as a machine
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructional objective: design computer use so the machine itself is not the focus; students focus on writing rather than on the hardware or inner workings of the computer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of four core objectives of the Purdue Calumet model: reduce students' attention to the computer as a machine so it functions transparently as a writing aid.

rubrics_metrics.name: View the computer as another tool
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat the computer like any other tool in the writing process rather than as a distinct or special subject of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model emphasizes positioning the computer alongside traditional tools (e.g., typewriter, pen) to support writing tasks and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the computer as a management tool to support, enhance, and improve writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage computer features to manage writing projects, drafts, revisions, and related workflow to improve overall writing quality and process efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit objective: employ computer capabilities (primarily word processing) to support management functions in PR writing courses—organizing documents, tracking revisions, coordinating group work, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance creativity in the classroom
rubrics_metrics.description: Use computer technology to foster and increase student creativity in public relations writing tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as a primary objective of the instructional model: computer use should expand creative possibilities rather than constrain them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize tool use over learning computer programming
rubrics_metrics.description: Course emphasis should be on using the computer as a practical writing tool rather than teaching students how to program or deeply technical computer skills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract explicitly recommends focusing on end-use (word processing and writing support) rather than on learning computer programming; i.e., prioritize applied skills valuable for PR practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide open computing labs staffed with professional consultants for assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing assignments should be completed in open computing laboratories that have professional consultants available to assist students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reported instructional arrangement: open labs with professional consultants support students during assignment completion; student evaluations were very positive for this setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use word processing as primary computer technology
rubrics_metrics.description: Primarily employ word processing tools when integrating computer technology into PR writing instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The document cites word processing as the main enabling computer technology for improving writing processes (flexibility, drafting, editing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase flexibility in the writing process
rubrics_metrics.description: Computer technology should enable greater flexibility in drafting, revising, and organizing written material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract claim: computer technology (primarily word processing) enables students to improve the writing process through increased flexibility in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support development of management skills and teamwork
rubrics_metrics.description: Computer-assisted instruction should increase support for management-related skills and enable teamwork in PR writing tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract notes 'increased support of management skills and team work' as a benefit/goal of using computer technology in PR courses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure success by professional-quality student work and employability
rubrics_metrics.description: One measure of the program's effectiveness is that students produce highly professional work and are hired on the basis of their computer experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract reports agencies and corporations finding students produce professional work and that students have been employed because of their unique computer experience; student evaluations were very positive.
